Requesting changes. The period-counting and rounding fixes may be fine, but the cap/minimum change goes against the docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth.

Blocking issue: the PR description says the new `if fee > cap: return cap; return max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS)` logic was added only so `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` passes, and that nothing in the docs supports it. The docstring applies the one-fifth-of-balance cap after the minimum and says the cap always wins. The new code breaks that rule: whenever the computed fee is at or below the cap, it can return more than the cap. For example, `late_fee_cents(1800, 45)` returns 500 even though the cap is 360. Charging more than the documented cap is risky in fee code, since caps on small balances are often a policy or compliance rule.

Please keep the original `min(max(fee, MINIMUM), balance // 5)` ordering, which matches the docstring. If `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` then fails, raise the conflict with the team: either the test is wrong or the docstring needs updating because the business rule changed. Don't quietly implement behaviour that contradicts the spec.

The ceiling-based period calculation and the half-up rounding look reasonable, but please confirm the docstring actually specifies both before merging.

Also, please rewrite the PR description to drop the "Perfect! All tests are now passing ✅" opener and state the test/docstring conflict plainly.
